tips.comment: Keep on Cobbling ran a blinder to finish 2nd last time out and can build on that form under STD to get his head in front and enter the winner's enclosure.

Hard to recommend on sole flat run, but middle distance pedigree is related to numerous flat winners and a multiple NH winner. Shrewd training duo who are in very good form @ present, are tops here numerically/percentage wise last 5 seasons, making current 16/1 decent Ew value in the race.

The model I run has Groom De Cotte to win at 2.88, coming in ahead of Martalmix'jac in second and Getthepot in third. This has largely been driven by the fact Groom De Cotte has the highest RPR score, the highest OR, and good form having recently won a class 5 chasing handicap in March.
Pulled up in heavy ground at Fontwell in January and has obviously needed a break. Had a busy winter with some good performances and drops down in grade here and has a great chance.

Beaten a short head when runner-up over 3 furlongs shorter at Southwell on the 3rd of February, remains on the same mark and the third horse home (Ali Star Bert) has won subsequently to boost the form. He is a former course winner so this sharp track will suit and tries this longer trip for the first time.

Fifth at Hereford in February and did run a good race in that handicap chase over three miles. Grillon De Monty won in April a few years back at Huntington, and I do think eased in grade today that the outsider can win this handicap.
Blackacre finished second last time out and is carrying a fair amount of weight less than the main market rival. I can see SP being a lot closer to the favorite.
Jackpot Cash is very likable here. A win last time out, looks in great form, likes the ground, distance looks favorable, and the field hasn't produced any form like his. One for the acca.

A large chance is taken here given this mare's antics in the straight at Sedgefield. But when pushed by Bass, she knuckled down and went away from the pursuers again. In her run before, she ran on at Exeter, finishing 2 lengths down to a horse rated 114. She starts here off a mark 14lbs below that and thus has a chance. The favourite is short for a horse carrying 8lbs more than in their last hurdle win, and Neigh Botha comes back to this from chasing and 5lb higher than his last win. Small stake.

The model I run has simulated this race, and has Auntie Maggie coming in first, ahead of Jackpot Cash in second and Neigh Botha in third. This result has been driven by the relatively high RPR combined with considerably lower weight to carry than the other horses with a similar RPR. (10st. 2lbs compared to 12 st. for the favourite).

Has won a point to point in April a few years back and I do think Forever Walking can feature like his fourth at Wetherby in February. Unexposed over hurdles and I think the outsider of six can win this Handicap Hurdle.
Has been running well on the level and also has a good record when hurdling, twice a winner and placed 3 times from 8 starts. Gets a fair chunk of weight from the fav and that could swing it.

Still only 9, ALLMANKIND now finds himself in hunter chase races after winning the Old Roan at Aintree in 2021 and having reasonable success over fences. Best recent form on offer and class will prevail.
I'm taking on Allmankind here with Empire de Maulde, who made an eye-catching effort in second last time out. That looks better than the market leader's most recent form.

Between Me And U, this Michael Herrington runner comes up from the local yard not far from me with a decent chance in the first here at Musselburgh today. It has had a second wind operation after a poor run last time at Southwell. If returning to its earlier form, it can go close to gaining a second win for the yard.

Three times a winner here, twice over 7 furlongs and once over 9 furlongs. Beaten a short head over course and distance when runner-up in November 2024 off a mark of 65 and sent off favourite. Disappointed at Newcastle last time out but in need of the run following a 55-day break, and no surprise to see a return to form with proven form here.

Rainwater completely bombed at Doncaster last time despite being well backed, but that just didn’t look like him at all. He’s usually super reliable and now drops back to 1m, which should really suit with a strong pace likely. Still on a fair mark, and if that last run was just an off day, he’s got every chance of bouncing back.

7yo gelding English Spirit usually goes well on faster turf ground so he wouldn't mind if the ground drys out a bit more today. Is on a handy mark and knocked at the door in two of his last three races. Should be in the mix under jockey Jack Mitchell.

Jesmond Dawn did too much early and didn’t quite get home over 10f at Redcar, but she’s usually a reliable type and the drop back to 1m looks ideal. The yard’s in good form and has a solid record at Musselburgh (103 runs, 22 wins, 1.32 A/E, +20 @ 19% ROI), so she looks set to bounce back and should be right in the mix.

Race 1 at Musselburgh today is the Enter ITV7 For Free Handicap (Class 5) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 1,611 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 8-year-old gelding Shine On Brendan from the James Sloan Goldie yard and will be ridden by Kaiya Fraser. This son of Society Rock is a 9-time winner and is usually a very consistent runner. The gelding is vying for his hat-trick today and is surely a strong contender in this field.

Twice a winner over 7f and 1 mile back in 2024, the last one in a much better class of race than this at Goodwood when trained by Richard Hannon. Form regressed after that and is now 40 lbs down the handicap since those days, and a revival is not out of the question at this level.

One that catches the eye in the first race at Musselburgh is the Ian Jardine-trained IZZARI, who hasn't been seen since December when disappointing at Southwell when sent off a well-backed 2/1 favourite. He had previously won well at Newcastle when closing from the back, and this contest looks wide open.

SPUN TO GOLD formerly trained by Andrew Balding is no doubt a well treated horse and given the current form of the yard his absence may not be an issue. He is by Justify a leading American sire who was top-class , so back down in class ahead of his reappearance could see him to good effect.

Sheikh Rashid Dalmook Al Maktoum’s huge 73% SR (A/E 1.83) with unraced favourites over sprint trips plus his 51% SR (A/E 1.29) with Irish-born favourites makes CLEAR FORCE really easy to back here at 5/6.

Only Spoofing didn’t get the clearest run at Bellewstown but wasn’t beaten far and hinted that he might be finding his level again. He’s looked regressive overall but this isn’t a strong race and the yard doesn’t send many over but when they do, it’s usually worth paying attention (30 runs, 10 wins, 1.64 A/E, +30pts @ 101% ROI). One to keep on side at the right price.

Zarzyni has twice before tasted success over today's course and distance. His first run of the season was on the all-weather where he finished fifth. He is back on turf at a track he appears to run well at and has a decent draw. So from only three pounds higher than his last winning mark, hopefully Zarzyni will make his presence felt under the horsemanship of Connor Beasley.

ETERNAL SUNSHINE has multiple wins in lower class sprints and still only a five year old mare she could be at her peak as a racehorse now. She has an often favoured high draw at this venue for five furlongs and there is good reason to think she can show up well here.

Alligator Alley is an 8 times career sprint winner who was winning in much better class of races than this back in 2023. Finished a close 4th on stable debut at Newcastle last month and is very well treated on old form and should run well if building on that last run.

A wide-open sprint where Knicks appeals at a big 11/1. He ran well on his seasonal reappearance at Doncaster and will be spot on for this. He also has a middle to high draw, which is advantageous here.

One win and three places in the last four starts last season. Decent effort when finishing two and a half lengths back on seasonal reappearance at Doncaster last month. Likely to be better for that run and looks a big price for each-way purposes here with a favorable low draw and with many bookies paying out on extra places.

Has been keeping good company and this represents a drop in class so must be respected off this mark. Was second beaten a head over C&D on this card last season on seasonal debut to a Group horse in Equality from a poor draw. Much lower now and as was second off this mark at Haydock too in September looks well handicapped and should go close despite advancing years. Yard going okay and have had a couple of winners from just eight runners sent out since the beginning of March. Speedy sort who likes the ground, has gone well fresh and has been operating at a higher level. Must go close from a fair draw.

Ziggys Queen didn’t get a clear run last time at Southwell but still finished close, and the return to this sharper trip looks a plus. She’s a C&D winner and has dropped to a mark she can definitely win off. If things open up for her, she’s entitled to go very close.

Castan has two course runs so far, which have brought about a win and narrowly been beaten by a nose. Both runs were on today's conditions. Has a nice low draw and has won off this mark before. Rattled off a hat trick on the all-weather in February and looks too big a price not to have an each-way interest back on turf.
Moon Flight has not been great since the return from a break in February but has dropped to his last winning mark and could be worth an Each Way with 5P on offer.

The 6-year-old recorded 6 wins from 20 outings last year, showcasing his capabilities. He recently finished a respectable 6th among 11 competitors in a handicap at Newcastle just 22 days ago. With odds of 25/1, there's excellent value in an each-way wager on this proven distance winner.

Sugar Baby runs off quite a low handicap rating of 61. Won over course and distance from OR58 in 2022. Beaten a neck here in 2023 off OR70. Winner on penultimate start at Newcastle back in February. The seven year-old Monsieur Bond gelding looks on good terms in this handicap. Carries 8 stone 6 pounds. Nice enough draw in stall 11. Sees this trip out well. Chance.

Back on turf, up two pounds following an all-weather win. Great chance, but only a monkey brain bets in these races as they are so tricky. Pass me a banana, somebody. I think it may well be a decent bet. Breeding and ground should suit the track. I don't know, it can be tricky.
In good form last year, winning 3 handicaps, 2 of them over this trip. Still only a 4-year-old and looks likely to improve again this season. Can go well fresh, so looks a live contender today.

Letsbefrank was gutsy when just getting up at Pontefract over 2m1f and now drops back in trip, which isn’t ideal but won’t rule him out. He’s got a top jockey-trainer combo in handicaps for the track (118 runs, 26 wins, 1.25 A/E, +24pts @ 21% ROI) and the yard’s in solid form, so even if he’s not fully wound up, he should still be in the mix.

This C/D winner put up another good effort under same conditions on final start of last season, so cleary goes well here. Has form @ this class 4 level, good apprentice retains ride taking off 3lb and very wiley trainer who is in very good form @ present, tops here numerically last 5 seasons and best here with his 4yo plus in same period, making current 14/1 very good Ew value in the race.

CASCADE HALL has stamina in the family which could make him a suitable candidate for a middle-distance test now tackling handicap company. He gets to take his chance with the yard in fine form often doing especially well at the scottish venues , so a big run could be on the cards.

Simple Star was never involved at Newcastle on his return but that was over a trip short of his best and off a break. He’s much better back up in distance and has run well at Musselburgh before. The yard tends to go well in spring handicaps (455 runs, 54 wins, 1.04 A/E, +75pts @ 17% ROI) and doesn’t get much betting attention, so he’s one to keep on side at a nice price if bouncing back.
Tafsir has a good record of running here of 1121, and although up 5 lbs for the latest win in September, she gets Amie in the saddle claiming 3 lbs and could be worth an EW 4P.

Spartan Warrior is a versatile horse, having run on the all-weather, over hurdles, and on the flat. His two wins have come on the flat at Beverley at a mile and a quarter and a mile and a half. His last race was the first of 2025 on the flat, where he finished nearer last than first over a trip that was probably too far. Today he is back down to one and a half miles with only an extra pound on his back than when winning at Beverley last year. Connor Beadsley gets his first ride on him, so hopefully, that is a significant indicator Spartan Warrior will run well.

Races form out of the handicap today, but interesting nevertheless off this mark with J P Sullivan on board. Course-winning form is always an attraction, and this horse arrives here today on the back of a good reappearance effort last time, for which he ought to be all the better today.

Marhaba Ghaiyyath finished second on debut at Wolverhampton in November before winning two Class 5 races at Lingfield in December and again at Wolverhampton last month. She looks on a fair mark for her handicap debut, and if she handles turf okay, she looks hard to beat.

I Am Me didn’t show much at Dundalk last time but had shaped well on debut and is generally a consistent sort. Stays this trip fine and while the mark looks a touch high for now, the trainer and jockey have a good record together in turf handicaps (139 runs, 35 wins, 1.19 A/E, +10pts @ 7% ROI), so she’s not one to write off just yet.
Drops down in grade after a good nursery second place last time and in his first race since being gelded. Mark reduced by a pound. Can be close to place money.

Was a dual winner on the Aw for M. Bell as a 2yo and did the same on stable debut for this operation. They then put up a good performance in a decent nursery on turf @ York. Very keen on 3yo comeback run @ Southwell, but will strip a lot fitter for that run. Good jockey who was on board for stable win back up and shrewd dual trainer has an excellent record @ this course with all his runners last 5 seasons, making current 18/1 solid Ew value in the race.

Just five career runs for the 3yo, beaten 3L or less in four of his races. The form from his last two turf runs looks decent. Debut for a new yard today and improvement possible after 7 months off the track. On a fair mark and the jockey’s 5lb claim today can help his chances. Looks overpriced.
Stockpyle was a decent second when second up and dropping to C4 7f for a new yard last month. He could go one better this time while up just 2 lbs for that.

Did not win in 2024 but ran some good races in defeat and has put up 2 decent comeback runs on Aw @ Southwell, so will be fitter than most. Is now 9lb lower than last winning mark so is very well handicapped @ this class 4 level, good jockey who is not normally associated with this stable, back up and very wiley trainer who is in very good form @ present, best here with his 4yo plus last 5 seasons, making current 7.50 very good Ew value in the race.
Led until inside the final furlong over a mile at Chelmsford last time out and will try to make all again today with the drop in trip aiding that cause.
Sondad, running for M&D Easterby, has only ever had 5 runs and has won twice. He has had a 227-day break, so he should have progressed. If he is ready to roll, he has a decent chance.
Vince Le Prince won last time out and is still treated fairly well and can go close again. The price is currently 6s, so it offers money back in the places.
This should have been my NAP. Definite chance if first-time blinkers have a positive effect. Has run well and placed at higher marks and is only a pound heavier than in his last winning mark.

NEW IMAGE has good turf form and has won here over 7f previously. Reappearing for the first time this campaign, and he won when favourite 4/5 times in 2024 including a win first time out. Hopefully this Frankel gelding can repeat a winning start this year.

A 3-time career winner all over 7f. The first one was over 7f at Newmarket back in April of last year when clocking a fast time. Has won 2 of the 4 starts this year, both times at Southwell in impressive style. Did not seem to get home last time out in the Spring Mile handicap at Doncaster last month with cut in the ground, having travelled well and faded inside the final furlong. Much better suited by the drop back to 7f here and looks capable of a bold show.

Spirit Genie didn’t get a clear shot at things last time at Doncaster and is better than that run suggests. This is his second go after a wind op, and the drop back in trip should suit much better. He goes well on soft ground and with a strong trainer-jockey combo (20 runs, 5 wins, 1.48 A/E, +12pts @ 61% ROI), he’s not without a chance.

Gweedore hasn’t been at his best in three runs this year but was a different horse in 2023 and is now back on a workable mark. Trainer’s in form, the jockey combo does well in turf handicaps (58 runs, 10 wins, 1.15 A/E, +11pts @ 19% ROI), and there’s been a nibble of overnight support. If he can rediscover that old spark, he’s got a real shout.
Dain Ma Nut is returning off the back of a hat trick and is weighted really nicely here. Paying 3 places here at a price to return stake.

Race 7 at Musselburgh today is the Sky Bet For The Fans Handicap (Class 2) for 4-year-olds and upwards over 1,421 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 4-year-old gelding Oriental Prince from the James Sloan Goldie yard, and will be ridden by Amie Waugh. This son of Orientor is in excellent form, winning 6 of his last 8 starts and won his hat-trick last time out. Cannot ignore here.
